## Summary

- add idempotent, credential-free Atlas/Argus tenant and least-privilege role provisioning SQL
- validate the canonical `homelab-postgres` identity and temporary `atlas-postgres` compatibility alias

- add logical backup tooling for Atlas, Argus, and credential-free cluster globals, with checksum manifests
- add a strictly read-only 7 daily / 5 weekly / 12 monthly retention planner that emits sanitized keep/expiration evidence without renaming, truncating, deleting, chmodding, or rewriting filesystem entries
- add isolated Atlas/Argus scratch restore verification for schema, row counts, integrity, read paths, and migration compatibility
- expose sanitized recovery freshness and last-restore evidence through authenticated admin health detail
- fail closed for schema-changing promotion when recovery evidence is absent, malformed, stale, incomplete, future-dated, or failed

- [x] Provisioning SQL is idempotent in disposable PostgreSQL 16
- [x] Atlas and Argus runtime roles are denied cross-tenant database access
- [x] Backup artifacts omit role password verifiers and validate checksum manifests before restore
- [x] Backup roots are required to be canonical absolute paths outside live PGDATA
- [x] Retention policy selects 7 daily, 5 weekly, and 12 monthly owned snapshots
- [x] Retention planning is bounded, sanitized, anomaly-detecting, and filesystem-read-only
- [x] Restore targets require explicit validated disposable Atlas and Argus names and are cleaned on exit
- [x] Import is dry-run-first, conflict-refusing, idempotent, and verifies convergence
- [x] Administrative evidence is bounded and omits paths, hosts, users, scratch names, manifest hashes, and credentials
- [x] Schema-changing promotion fails closed on stale or invalid evidence

## Production-only gates — intentionally unresolved

- [ ] Production tenant and role provisioning approved and completed
- [ ] Production `homelab-postgres` identity and `atlas-postgres` alias approved and validated
- [ ] Production import reconciliation approved and completed
- [ ] Production backup schedule approved and enabled

- [ ] Production backup destination verified outside live PGDATA and covered by separate storage protection
- [ ] Production isolated restore approved and verified
- [ ] Production schema-promotion evidence reviewed

Issue #40 remains open. This draft adds operator controls and evidence for separately authorized production work; it intentionally does not implement or authorize production retention deletion, reclamation, or scheduling.

title: fix(extraction): normalize Trafilatura results
body:
## Summary

- add one allowlisted normalization boundary for Trafilatura 2.x `Document` and mapping results
- route primary extraction, authenticated extraction, residential extraction, Archive.is, Wayback, and MCP archive recovery through it
- preserve Argus-owned provenance by admitting only text, title, author, and date
- correct the final fallback state so quality-passed but incomplete content is not mislabeled `all_extractors_quality_failed`

## Root cause

Trafilatura 2.x returns a `Document` by default, while most Argus callers still assumed a dictionary. Only the primary extractor had an inline conversion, so the other paths either raised or silently fell back. The audited substantial-content observation was also reproducible independently: completeness correctly requested later fallbacks, but when they failed the final branch overwrote the earlier successful quality decision.

## Behavior

Completeness still runs the full fallback chain for likely truncation. If no later extractor recovers a complete result, Argus now returns the best quality-approved result with its incomplete assessment intact. Content that fails the minimum-content or other quality gates remains rejected.

No provider enablement, paid extraction, SSRF behavior, URL redaction, privacy control, or spend control changed.

## Verification

- focused extraction, residential, MCP, and quality suites: `103 passed`
- full suite: `423 passed, 6 skipped`
- four pre-existing Starlette cookie deprecation warnings only
- Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed

Closes #43

title: fix(extraction): make Playwright lifecycle safe
body:
## Summary

- serialize shared Playwright browser initialization
- stop and clear a started runtime when Chromium launch fails
- cache the unavailable capability until an explicit reset
- make context/page and FastAPI shutdown cleanup lifecycle-safe
- add focused lifecycle, recovery, concurrency, shutdown, and real missing-browser process tests

## Root cause

When `async_playwright().start()` succeeded but `chromium.launch()` failed, Argus returned without stopping the runtime or caching the missing capability. Every later extraction repeated the start/fail/leak cycle until the 512 MiB container OOM-restarted.

## Validation

- `ARGUS_AUTOLOAD_DOTENV=false uv run pytest -q tests/test_playwright_lifecycle.py` — 7 passed
- `ARGUS_AUTOLOAD_DOTENV=false uv run pytest -q` — 356 passed, 4 pre-existing Starlette deprecation warnings

- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`
- independent task review: spec compliant, quality approved, no findings

## Remaining gate

Docker is unavailable on the development Mac, so the sanitized 512 MiB container canary was not run. Production deployment/canary authorization is deliberately not implied by this PR. Issue 22 should remain open until that evidence is recorded.

- [ ] SearXNG compatibility access is loopback-only and removed after known direct callers migrate.

title: Promote immutable homelab releases with rollback proof
body:
## Parent

[Wayfinder: make Argus a reliable homelab retrieval platform for Maya](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/23)

## What to build

Replace mutable-tag and OCI-jump deployment with one serialized, digest-addressed promotion transaction. Build once, attest once, admit the exact image through isolated gates, cut over one authority, and restore the previous compatible digest automatically when blocking checks fail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] GitHub Actions builds one frozen image, captures its manifest digest and source commit, publishes provenance and an SBOM, and never rebuilds the production candidate.
- [ ] Workflow actions are pinned by full commit SHA and permissions are least privilege.
- [ ] A protected production environment uses one non-canceling concurrency group and an ephemeral, narrowly permitted Tailscale deployment identity.
- [ ] Standard SSH initially uses a pinned host key and forced-command key; OCI and `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` are absent.
- [ ] One root-owned idempotent homelab promoter serializes with a host-local lock and records requested, current, previous, and known-good digests outside Argus containers.
- [ ] An isolated candidate uses scratch PostgreSQL, no production ingress, no Maya dispatcher, and no paid credentials while running identity, search, extraction, MCP, accounting, dependency-loss, restart, and resource gates.
- [ ] Schema-changing releases require fresh backup/restore proof and verification that the previous image accepts the new schema or an explicit forward-repair plan.
- [ ] Production cutover verifies actual loaded digest and identity, then observes a 30-minute soak.
- [ ] A blocking failure restores the exact previous compatible digest and reruns the same readiness, identity, and canary proof.

- [Make Argus configuration and image CI hermetic](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/32)

title: Reserve and reconcile paid-provider spending durably

## What to build

Make provider routing and usage accounting crash-safe. Paid work must reserve a conservative provider-specific maximum before the external attempt, settle to a known charge afterward, and retain uncertain consumption until authoritative reconciliation or explicit operator action.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every paid-provider attempt durably reserves its conservative maximum before the provider can consume credit.
- [ ] Known outcomes atomically settle reservations to the actual provider charge and preserve the attempt audit record.
- [ ] Unknown crash or timeout outcomes remain visible uncertain charges that reduce available budget and never expire into an automatic refund.
- [ ] Provider-authoritative reconciliation and explicit operator resolution are idempotent, authenticated, and audited.
- [ ] Free and local attempts record outcome and usage without creating monetary reservations.
- [ ] Usage, budget, and balance interfaces work on PostgreSQL and distinguish Argus estimates from provider snapshots with source and freshness.
- [ ] Caller identity and tier caps derive from scoped credentials; a supplied caller label is retained only as diagnostic context.
- [ ] Fault-injection tests cover crashes before attempt, after provider acceptance, during settlement, and during reconciliation.

title: Persist extraction and session operations in the authoritative ledger
body:
## Parent

[Wayfinder: make Argus a reliable homelab retrieval platform for Maya](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/23)

## What to build

Extend the authoritative persistence slice through extraction and multi-turn sessions so useful retrieval operations survive restart and every production usage surface reads PostgreSQL through the same repository interfaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extraction runs, extractor attempts, normalized outcomes, provenance, artifact metadata, content hashes, latency, and safe failure summaries persist transactionally.
- [ ] Multi-turn session state uses the shared persistence interface and remains correct across restart.
- [ ] Direct SQLite-only usage, session, and extraction query paths are removed from production code.
- [ ] Administrative usage counts search and extraction runs rather than result rows and produces consistent answers on PostgreSQL and SQLite.
- [ ] Tests cover failed extraction, fallback attempts, session continuation, transaction rollback, and restart recovery.
- [ ] Existing durable history has a documented, idempotent import and reconciliation path.

## Blocked by

- [Record accepted search retrievals transactionally in PostgreSQL](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/33)

title: Record accepted search retrievals transactionally in PostgreSQL
body:
## Parent

[Wayfinder: make Argus a reliable homelab retrieval platform for Maya](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/23)

## What to build

Land the first complete PostgreSQL-backed retrieval slice. A search accepted by Argus must commit its request, run, provider attempts, normalized results, provenance, and required delivery intent through one persistence interface before the response is acknowledged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Versioned Alembic migrations create the Argus search ledger in a separate PostgreSQL database without direct table creation at runtime.
- [ ] The HTTP search path writes the request, search run, provider attempts, normalized results, provenance, and content identities through SQLAlchemy repository interfaces.
- [ ] Argus does not claim a retrieval was durably accepted when the required transaction fails.
- [ ] SQLite remains a supported development and standalone adapter and passes the same repository contract tests.
- [ ] PostgreSQL concurrency and rollback tests prove partial attempts or results cannot be acknowledged as a complete accepted retrieval.
- [ ] An idempotent legacy-state import or reconciliation command reports source, imported, skipped, and conflicting row counts without mutating production by default.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
